description: Self-hosted geospatial data catalog with semantic search (pgvector), OGC/STAC APIs, and map builder. Built on FastAPI, PostGIS, React, and MapLibre.

latest_release.name: v1.31.0
latest_release.body:
An instance on 1.30.1 moves to 1.31.0 with one additive migration (0103,
which allows the `database` source format), and releases back to 1.29.2 keep
serving while it runs. SQL Server import stays off until an operator sets
`DATABASE_SOURCES`. Overlays must declare `EXTENSION_API_VERSION` 23.

### Added
- The aggregate endpoint takes `blank_text_as_null` for `value_counts` and `group_by`, counting a text column's empty strings with its NULLs. Dashboard widgets use it, so a category stored as both reads as one "(no value)" row. Whitespace-only text keeps its own key.
- Database connections: an operator lists SQL Server databases in `DATABASE_SOURCES`, `GET /services/databases/{connection}/tables/` lists a connection's spatial tables and views with their geometry column, type and SRID for users who can create datasets, and `/capabilities/` names each connection and its database for those users. The API image now includes the FreeTDS ODBC driver (`tdsodbc`). The setting is refused in `multi_tenant` mode.
- Database import and refresh: `POST /services/databases/{connection}/imports/` copies one listed table or view into a new dataset as an ingest job, and the dataset's Refresh reads it again by connection name. The dataset's origin is `database`, with `source_format` `database`, no `source_url` and an `origin_uri` of `database://<connection>/<schema>.<table>`; the table's SRID is read from SQL Server, and a table with SRID 0 or no rows asks for `srid_override`. A second import of the same table by the same user answers 409 `duplicate_source`. A refresh is verified under the `database_single_read_v1` policy: a removed or retyped column and an empty read over a copy that has rows wait for review, and a refresh through a connection that is no longer configured fails naming it. The `OriginKind` request enum and refresh runs' `origin_kind` gain `database`.
- Add Data has a Database source when a connection is configured: pick a connection and a table, give a table without an SRID its CRS, and import. Each listed table now carries `importable`, and a name GeoLens can't import is shown but disabled. A database dataset's Source tab shows its connection and table, refreshes it, and can accept a refresh held for review. `geolens replace` refuses a database dataset, and the MCP client reports the `database` origin.

### Changed
- The backend image no longer installs the FastAPI CLI extras (`fastapi[standard]`): the `fastapi` command, Jinja2 and `pydantic-extra-types` are gone, and Uvicorn is a direct dependency. Operators building their own images should start the API with `uvicorn`, as the bundled Compose files do.
- Overlay authors: `EXTENSION_API_VERSION` is now 23. `CatalogPort` gains the
  required `queue_ingest_job()` and `refresh_database_task()`.
- The viewer legend describes a clustered layer as "Grouped into clusters as you zoom out" or "Shown as individual points" instead of "Server cluster", "Bounded cluster" and "Point fallback".

### Fixed
- Dashboards: an indicator's difference no longer shows decimals that the rounding of its value hides, so a value of 1,408 against a reference of 1,239 reads 169, not 169.38.
- Map viewer: with an AI provider configured, the "Ask AI" button no longer covers the expanded attribution; the attribution sits above it.
- A DEM dataset whose extent the reader cannot see now frames its preview to the bounds in its tile token instead of opening at world zoom and timing out; with no bounds either it shows "Preview unavailable" at once.
- Visiting `/stories` opens the Stories tab of the Maps page instead of a 404.
- A user can no longer end up with two copies of one service layer or database table. A second import while the first is still queued or running answers 409 `duplicate_source` with `existing_job_id` in place of `existing_dataset_id` and `existing_title`. Retrying a failed import answers the same 409 while the job's owner holds a copy of its source, and works again once that copy is deleted. A

detail.readme:
GeoLens

A self-hosted spatial data catalog and map builder that keeps track of where every dataset came from.

Live demo · Install · Documentation · Connect QGIS or code · Discussions

[English](README.md) · [Español](README.es.md) · [Français](README.fr.md) · [Deutsch](README.de.md) · [简体中文](README.zh.md) [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/geolens-io/geolens?style=flat-square&label=release)](https://github.com/geolens-io/geolens/releases/latest) [![CI status](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/geolens-io/geolens/ci.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=CI)](https://github.com/geolens-io/geolens/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: Apache-2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-2563eb?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![OpenSSF Scorecard](https://api.securityscorecards.dev/projects/github.com/geolens-io/geolens/badge)](https://securityscorecards.dev/viewer/?uri=github.com/geolens-io/geolens) [![OpenSSF Best Practices](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/15857/badge)](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/15857)


Manhattan's buildings at their surveyed roof heights, colored by construction era, with the subway network. Browse the demo's maps.

GeoLens is for teams whose spatial data is spread across file shares, PostGIS databases, web services and STAC catalogs. It puts that data in one searchable catalog, records where each dataset came from and checks whether the source is still current. Teams build and share maps in the browser, and QGIS, scripts and AI agents read the same data through OGC API and STAC. It runs on your own servers with Docker Compose, sends no telemetry and is licensed under Apache 2.0. The [demo](https://demo.getgeolens.com) needs no install or account; sign in with Google, GitHub or Microsoft to use the map builder. Demo data may be wiped at any time. ## A closer look

Search by meaning: "where storms hit the coast" finds hurricane tracks and coastal exposure layers.
Each dataset has a page with its metadata and source, plus a map preview when it has an extent.

Before you import a service layer, GeoLens previews its columns and first rows.
Each replacement is recorded in the history, and you can restore the previous version.

Layers render as points, symbols, heatmaps or clusters, and the ramp list can be limited to colorblind-safe ones.
3D terrain from your own elevation data, here the Matterhorn from swissALTI3D lidar.

Sentinel-2 scenes referenced from a STAC catalog. The imagery stays where it is and is tiled on request.
Keep a map to yourself, open it to your team, or make it public with a link and embed code.

The admin overview shows service health next to dataset and storage totals.
Viewer, editor and admin roles, with each capability switched on or off per role.
## How it fits together ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph IN ["Bring data in"] F["Files
GeoPackage · Shapefile · GeoParquet
GeoTIFF · COPC · 3D Tiles"] DB["Existing PostGIS tables"] SVC["Services
ArcGIS · WFS · OGC API Features"] ST["Remote STAC assets"] end subgraph GL ["GeoLens"] CAT["Catalog
search · metadata · provenance"] MB["Map builder
styles · 3D · analysis · stories · dashboards · sharing"] STD["Open APIs
OGC API · STAC · DCAT · tiles"] end subgraph OUT ["Use it anywhere"] WEB["Browsers and embeds"] GIS["QGIS · ArcGIS · CesiumJS"] CODE["curl · Python · TypeScript · DuckDB"] AG["AI agents via MCP"] end F & DB & SVC & ST --> CAT CAT --> MB --> WEB CAT --> STD --> GIS & CODE & AG ``` ## One catalog for scattered data - Upload Shapefile, GeoPackage, GeoJSON, GeoParquet, FlatGeobuf, KML/KMZ, zipped File Geodatabase, CSV, Excel or GeoTIFF (converted to Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF). 3D Tiles and COPC point clouds are hosted for CesiumJS, QGIS and Potree. - Serve tables already in GeoLens's PostGIS database in place, import WFS, ArcGIS and OGC API Features layers and refresh them on demand, or reference remote STAC assets without copying them. - Draw new datasets in the browser. - Find data with fuzzy search, or by meaning once an embedding provider is configured. Filter by type, place and time, group datasets into collections, edit metadata and restore a dataset's previous version after a replacement. ## Know where every dataset came from


A dataset imported from the USGS earthquake service.

Each dataset records where it came from: an uploaded file, a database table, a service, a STAC item or a drawing in the browser. Imported datasets also record when they were last refreshed, and with an update cadence GeoLens marks them fresh, due or overdue. For services and STAC sources, GeoLens also checks that the source still answers, and for services it flags upstream schema changes before they reach your maps. If a service disappears, the imported copy keeps working. ## Build and share maps - Point, symbol, heatmap, cluster, line, arrow, fill, 3D extrusion, raster and hillshade layers, with data-driven styles, labels, icons, patterns, filters and popups. Terrain comes from your own elevation models. - Buffer, centroid, clip, dissolve, spatial join, select by location, measure and intersect. Most operations preview on the map, and each result is saved as a new dataset, from the builder or the CLI. - Story maps walk readers through a map scene by scene, with Markdown text, images, buttons and separators. Dashboards put indicators, charts, filters and Markdown notes beside a map. A Map data panel shows the rows behind each layer, as a table or a list. - Public maps and published stories show their title and image when pasted into Slack, Teams or social posts, and maps embed in other sites with private tokens. - The interface is in English, Spanish, French, German and Simplified Chinese. ## Use the data from anywhere Vector datasets are OGC API Features collections, the catalog is OGC API Records and STAC, and every layer has a tile URL. You can try this against the demo without an account (the second command needs `jq`): ```sh # Search the catalog (OGC API Records) curl "https://demo.getgeolens.com/api/collections/datasets/items?q=volcanic%20eruptions" # Read the top match with a CQL2 filter (OGC API Features): eruptions of VEI 6 or larger ID=$(curl -s "https://demo.getgeolens.com/api/collections/datasets/items?q=volcanic%20eruptions&limit=1" | jq -r '.features[0].id') curl -G "https://demo.getgeolens.com/api/collections/$ID/items" \ --data-urlencode "filter=vei >= 6" -d limit=3 ``` QGIS adds the same API as an OGC API Features connection, as the [QGIS guide](https://docs.getgeolens.com/guides/api/qgis/) shows. The [GeoLens plugin for QGIS](https://github.com/geolens-io/qgis-geolens-plugin) adds catalog search, private datasets and edits that sync back to GeoLens.


QGIS reading the demo over OGC API Features, without a plugin.

| Standard | Where | Use it with | |---|---|---| | OGC API Features, with CQL2 filtering and queryables | `/api/collections/{id}/items` | QGIS, ArcGIS, GDAL/OGR and other OGC API clients | | OGC API Records | `/api/collections/datasets/items` | Catalog search from other portals and tools | | STAC API 1.0 | `/api/stac/` | STAC clients such as pystac-client and STAC Browser | | DCAT 3, DCAT-US 3.0 and GeoDCAT-AP as JSON-LD | `/api/datasets/dcat/`, `/api/datasets/dcat-us/3.0/`, `/api/datasets/geodcat-ap/` | Harvesting into national and EU open-data portals | | Vector tiles and COG raster tiles | a tile URL on every layer | MapLibre, OpenLayers, Leaflet | | 3D Tiles and COPC | each 3D dataset's page | CesiumJS, QGIS, Potree | Data exports as GeoJSON, Shapefile, GeoPackage, CSV, FlatGeobuf, GeoParquet, PMTiles or Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF. The `geolens` CLI publishes files and applies catalog manifests, Python and TypeScript SDKs cover the API, and an MCP server lets AI agents search the catalog and, with a `map_author` API key, create and style maps. The [API reference](https://docs.getgeolens.com/guides/api/) and [SDK guides](https://docs.getgeolens.com/guides/sdk/) document them, and the [examples gallery](https://geolens-io.github.io/geolens-examples/) has runnable code for MapLibre, Leaflet, OpenLayers, the ArcGIS Maps SDK, QGIS and DuckDB. ## Optional AI


"How many of these hurricanes made landfall?" returns the count, a table and the assumption the answer rests on.

GeoLens can answer questions about a dataset, edit maps from plain-language requests, draft metadata and search in natural language. It works with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including a local server such as Ollama, and with Claude through Anthropic, Microsoft Foundry, Amazon Bedrock or Google Vertex AI. AI stays off until an administrator configures a provider, and every workflow works without it. ## Install You need Git, curl and Docker with the Compose plugin. The [Install Guide](https://docs.getgeolens.com/guides/quickstart/install/) lists the versions, memory and ports it expects. ```sh curl -fsSL https://getgeolens.com/install.sh | sh # clone, generate secrets, start the stack cd geolens grep '^GEOLENS_ADMIN_PASSWORD=' .env # the generated admin password ``` Open http://localhost:8080 and sign in as `admin` with that password. Each [release](https://github.com/geolens-io/geolens/releases) includes a `SHA256SUMS` file for checking `install.sh` before you run it. To build from source instead, clone the repository and run `bash scripts/install.sh`; the first build takes 5-10 minutes. For production, read the [cloud deployment guide](https://docs.getgeolens.com/guides/quickstart/cloud-deployment/), which also lists what an external database needs. Docker Compose is the supported path, and [geolens-deployments](https://github.com/geolens-io/geolens-deployments) has a community-maintained Helm chart and Terraform recipes for AWS ECS Fargate and Azure Container Apps. The bundled database is backed up daily, and the [backup guide](https://docs.getgeolens.com/guides/admin/backups/) covers off-site copies and restores. [UPGRADING.md](UPGRADING.md) covers upgrades and rollback, [RUNBOOK.md](RUNBOOK.md) covers operations, and the [Configuration Reference](https://docs.getgeolens.com/guides/quickstart/configuration/) lists every setting. ## Your first dataset With the [CLI](https://docs.getgeolens.com/guides/cli/) installed, publish the sample file from the install directory: ```sh geolens login http://localhost:8080/api # your admin username and password geolens publish examples/manifests/first-catalog/city-parks.geojson --name "City Parks" ``` `geolens publish` prints the new dataset's URL. To manage a whole catalog, describe the sources in a `geolens.yaml` manifest and run `geolens apply`; [`examples/manifests/`](examples/manifests/) has templates. To load the demo's maps and datasets, export `GEOLENS_ADMIN_PASSWORD` from `.env` and run `python scripts/seed-showcase.py --username admin`. The script needs Python 3.10+ and `httpx` and downloads public data from about a dozen sources; [scripts/README.md](scripts/README.md) has the sizes and options. ## Privacy and access - GeoLens sends no telemetry. Apart from the default basemap tiles and the remote services or STAC sources your users register, it makes outbound calls only for features an administrator turns on. [EGRESS.md](EGRESS.md) lists them and explains how to run air-gapped. - Your data stays readable without GeoLens. Vector datasets are ordinary PostGIS tables in a `data` schema, rasters are Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs in your own storage (local disk, S3/MinIO or Azure Blob), and the catalog exports through OGC API, STAC and DCAT. - Sign-in uses local accounts or OAuth 2.0/OIDC (Google, Microsoft, GitHub or a generic provider), with roles, per-dataset permissions, per-user API keys and an audit log. Self-registration is off by default. - Features released in this repository stay free. [EDITIONS.md](EDITIONS.md) describes the optional paid support and add-ons. ## Known limitations - The supported install, Docker Compose, runs on one host. For high availability, run several replicas of the API, worker, frontend and Titiler against a managed PostgreSQL with automatic failover, shared object storage and one Valkey or Redis cache. With Azure Blob or local storage, API and worker replicas also need a shared staging volume, since only S3 keeps uploads in the bucket. Local storage keeps every file on that volume, so Titiler replicas mount it too. [geolens-deployments](https://github.com/geolens-io/geolens-deployments) has a community-maintained Helm chart, Terraform recipes for AWS and Azure, and guides for AWS, Azure, Google Cloud and DigitalOcean. GeoLens itself doesn't cluster the database or read from replicas. - One organization per deployment. - Terrain rendering assumes elevation in meters; other vertical units render exaggerated. - GeoLens's own REST API can change between minor releases (the standards endpoints follow their specifications). The [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md) lists contract changes. When a change breaks callers, the old form keeps working for the later of the next minor release and 90 days, and the CHANGELOG records its removal date. That covers REST routes and fields, the map and dashboard JSON clients write, and CLI commands and flags; the SDKs follow the API, and MCP tool names and arguments aren't covered. ## Contributing Bug reports, fixes, translations and docs are welcome. [CONTRIBUTING](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) covers setup and tests, and [ARCHITECTURE](.github/ARCHITECTURE.md) maps the code. The [QGIS plugin](https://github.com/geolens-io/qgis-geolens-plugin), [examples](https://github.com/geolens-io/geolens-examples) and [deployments](https://github.com/geolens-io/geolens-deployments) repositories take issues and pull requests too. Ask questions in [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/geolens-io/geolens/discussions), report bugs in [Issues](https://github.com/geolens-io/geolens/issues), and report security problems privately as described in [SECURITY.md](.github/SECURITY.md). The [roadmap](https://docs.getgeolens.com/roadmap/) shows what's planned. ## Built on GeoLens is built on these open source projects. Thanks to everyone who maintains them. - [PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/) and [PostGIS](https://postgis.net/) hold the catalog and every vector dataset, and [pgvector](https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector) stores the embeddings behind search by meaning. - [GDAL](https://gdal.org/) reads the files and services GeoLens imports and writes the formats it exports, and [PROJ](https://proj.org/) handles coordinate transformations. - [TiTiler](https://developmentseed.org/titiler/) serves raster tiles from Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs. - [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/) serves the API, and [Procrastinate](https://procrastinate.readthedocs.io/) runs background jobs with PostgreSQL as the queue. - [MapLibre GL JS](https://maplibre.org/) draws the maps, [deck.gl](https://deck.gl/) and [loaders.gl](https://loaders.gl/) render 3D Tiles and point clouds, and [Terra Draw](https://terradraw.io/) handles drawing and editing. - The web app is written in [React](https://react.dev/). These names belong to their owners, and listing them doesn't mean they endorse GeoLens; see [TRADEMARKS.md](TRADEMARKS.md#other-projects-names). ## License GeoLens is licensed under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE). The GeoLens name, logo and brand assets are not covered by this license; see [TRADEMARKS.md](TRADEMARKS.md). Sample-data attribution is in [THIRD_PARTY_DATA.md](THIRD_PARTY_DATA.md). The web app serves the license notices for the code it bundles at `/third-party-licenses.txt`, and the backend image's copyleft notices are in [backend/licenses](backend/licenses/).
